# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act are now set to apply from **2 December 2027**, replacing the originally legislated date of 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). However, a small cluster of September 2026 sources claims this date has been pushed further to 2 August 2029 (high confidence by corroboration score, but from non-official domains with no EU confirmation) — a claim treated here as contested rather than established.

## Key Findings

### Current Applicable Date
Multiple official European Commission sources consistently state that obligations for high-risk systems listed in Annex III will enter into force on **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). This reflects a legislative change under the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification), which was adopted 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### How the Timeline Changed
Prior to the Omnibus amendment, the applicable date in law for Annex III high-risk provisions was **2 August 2026** (high confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). Separately, the European Parliament describes the originally adopted AI Act (June 2024) as providing for full applicability 24 months after entry into force and high-risk obligations 36 months after entry into force (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)); this 36-month figure is not reconciled in available sources with the 2 August 2026 date, since the Act's 1/2 August 2024 entry into force would imply a later date — this arithmetic inconsistency remains an open issue rather than a resolved fact. The Council and Parliament agreed on 7 May 2026 to a Commission proposal adjusting the timeline for high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning application on confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legal Text and Grandfathering
The consolidated EUR-Lex text (as of 27.07.2026) confirms that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before the applicable Chapter III date only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some service-desk guidance still references 2 August 2026 as the relevant grandfathering date under Article 111(2), suggesting possible inconsistency in how the amended timeline is reflected across EU guidance materials (medium confidence) ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
The deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) is **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). One lower-confidence source states this deadline as 2 August 2027 instead, a one-year discrepancy not resolved in this research (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

### A Disputed Further Delay
A set of September 2026 legal-analysis sources claims the Annex III deadline has been moved again, to **2 August 2029**, citing unready harmonised standards and notified bodies (high confidence per corroboration score, but from non-official domains, with no official EU source confirming it) ([legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [legal insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply)). Correspondingly, some sources state conformity assessment by notified bodies is not required until the applicable date — variably reported as 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2029 (medium confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Scope and Enforcement
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk, rather than being itself an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can trigger penalties up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, per some reporting up to €35 million (low confidence) ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Primary contradiction:** Official EU Commission sources state 2 December 2027; three non-official September 2026 sources claim 2 August 2029 (high confidence by corroboration metric, but unverified against any official source) — flagged as unresolved.
- **Secondary contradiction:** Some sources still reference 2 August 2026 as operative, likely reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus reporting.
- **Annex I deadline discrepancy:** 2 August 2028 (most sources) vs. 2 August 2027 (one low-confidence source).
- **Unresolved arithmetic issue:** European Parliament's "36 months after entry into force" claim (confidence below 0.4 for underlying derivation) does not clearly reconcile with the stated 2 August 2026 pre-Omnibus date.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether an amending regulation beyond the Omnibus exists establishing 2 August 2029.
- The exact legal citation and text of the Article 113 amendment.
- Whether harmonised standards and notified bodies will be ready by December 2027.
- The current authoritative consolidated Article 113 text as of late 2026.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act are now set to apply from **2 December 2027**, replacing the originally legislated date of 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). However, a small cluster of September 2026 sources claims this date has been pushed further to 2 August 2029, a claim not corroborated by any official EU source in this research (medium-high confidence, contested).

## Key Findings

### Current Applicable Date
Multiple official European Commission sources consistently state that obligations for high-risk systems listed in Annex III will enter into force on **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). This reflects a legislative change under the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification), which was adopted 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Regulatory Framework for AI](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### How the Timeline Changed
Originally, under the AI Act as adopted in June 2024, high-risk obligations were set to apply 36 months after entry into force, translating to **2 August 2026** (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). This 2 August 2026 date was widely cited prior to the Omnibus amendment as the applicable date in law for Annex III provisions (high confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). The Council and Parliament agreed on 7 May 2026 to a Commission proposal adjusting the timeline for high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning application on confirmation that necessary standards and tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legal Text and Grandfathering
The consolidated EUR-Lex text (as of 27.07.2026) confirms that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before the applicable Chapter III date only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Some service-desk guidance still references 2 August 2026 as the relevant grandfathering date under Article 111(2), suggesting possible inconsistency in how the amended timeline is reflected across EU guidance materials (medium confidence) ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Related Deadlines
The deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) is **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). One lower-confidence source states this deadline as 2 August 2027 instead, a one-year discrepancy not resolved in this research (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

### A Disputed Further Delay
A set of September 2026 legal-analysis sources claims the Annex III deadline has been moved again, to **2 August 2029**, citing unready harmonised standards and notified bodies (high confidence per corroboration score, but from non-official domains) ([legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [legal insights](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply)). Correspondingly, some sources state conformity assessment by notified bodies is not required until the applicable date — variably reported as 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2029 (medium confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Scope and Enforcement
Annex III lists eight categories of AI use cases that can be classified as high-risk, rather than being itself an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). Non-compliance with high-risk obligations can trigger penalties up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, per some reporting up to €35 million (low confidence) ([McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Primary contradiction:** Official EU Commission sources state 2 December 2027; three non-official September 2026 sources claim 2 August 2029. No official EU source in this dataset confirms the later date — flag as unverified (confidence below 0.4 threshold for underlying legal basis).
- **Secondary contradiction:** Some sources still reference 2 August 2026 as operative, likely reflecting outdated pre-Omnibus reporting.
- **Annex I deadline discrepancy:** 2 August 2028 (most sources) vs. 2 August 2027 (one low-confidence source).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether an amending regulation beyond the Omnibus exists establishing 2 August 2029.
- The exact legal citation and text of the Article 113 amendment.
- Whether harmonised standards and notified bodies will be ready by December 2027.
- The current authoritative consolidated Article 113 text as of late 2026.
